raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Closes #43196.

A main model and its MTP draft can share a checkpoint while requiring different weights. Existing model implementations usually filter unused tensors inside `load_weights`, after the Default Loader iterator or prefetcher has started processing files. On whole-file paths, an unnecessary shard may already have been read into memory before the model discards its tensors.

Following [vLLM #60152](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60152), this PR extracts existing model-owned selection rules into a reusable interface and excludes wholly unused shards before weight-payload reads and prefetch. This avoids unnecessary reads, memory copies, and tensor iteration.

The same need arose in [ModelExpress #805](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/modelexpress/issues/805). Keeping the rules in SGLang lets native loaders and downstream integrations share one implementation, instead of requiring MX to duplicate architecture-specific checkpoint naming rules and keep them synchronized with upstream changes.

## Modifications

1. **Model-owned weight selection.** Add an optional `is_unused_checkpoint_weight(name)` hook. It receives a raw checkpoint tensor name and returns `True` when the model does not use that weight. Pre-read selection and `load_weights` share the same rule, preserving shared weights and pipeline-parallel embedding requirements.
2. **Select files before Default Loader reads.** Pass the rule through `Source.is_unused_weight`, inspect safetensors headers, and retain a shard whenever it contains at least one required tensor. Apply selection before weight iteration and prefetch, preserving the original file order.
3. **Keep actual weight loading unchanged.** Renaming, quantization, fusion, parallel sharding, and parameter assignment remain in the existing model code. The generic loader has no model allowlist and does not assume an `mtp.` prefix.
4. **Preserve compatibility.** Models without the hook, non-safetensors formats, and name transformations that cannot safely map to raw checkpoint names keep their existing loading behavior. If selection rejects every shard, retain the original list so the model's existing missing-weight validation still runs.

The model adapters in this PR cover Qwen3-MoE, Qwen3-Next, Qwen3.5 (dense/MoE, including the text implementation), and Qwen4-Exp main/MTP loading. Qwen3.5 MTP selection preserves shared embedding weights.

Other architectures can opt in by extracting their existing `load_weights` skip rules into `is_unused_checkpoint_weight(name)`, while preserving required shared weights and quantization metadata. The same rule can then be reused by Default Loader and RunAI ModelStreamer without adding architecture-specific branches to the generic loaders.

Selection is at whole-shard granularity, not tensor-range granularity. Mixed shards containing both main and draft weights can still be selected by both roles.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Qwen benchmark record: 2026-10-13. The measurements below describe the tested configurations and loading paths.

### Default Loader: whole-file reads

H20×8, TP=8, with checkpoints prepared locally. The model completed one baseline/modified comparison pair with identical launch arguments on both sides, `--weight-loader-disable-mmap`, and two reader threads.

| Model | Load phase | Shards: baseline → this PR | TP0 load time: baseline → this PR |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3.5 MTP 122B | Main | 49 → 49 | 72.44s → 67.74s |
| Qwen3.5 MTP 122B | Draft | 49 → 1 | **64.32s → 9.58s** |

In this comparison pair, draft-load time decreased by **85.1%**. TP0 logical reads during draft loading decreased from **121.00 GiB to 8.38 GiB**.

Both configurations completed main/draft loading on all eight ranks, passed HTTP health checks, and completed two 32-token generation requests each.

Logical read counts come from process `rchar`, not physical disk or OSS traffic. Host page cache was not cleared for this pair. These results describe the local whole-file path and should not be interpreted as the benefit of the default mmap path.

### Default Loader: mmap

Qwen3.5 MTP 122B completed **five interleaved comparison pairs** with mmap enabled and checkpoint prefetch disabled. Before each engine launch, only the test-private checkpoint files were evicted from page cache, and `mincore` confirmed zero resident pages. Normal cache reuse between the main and draft loads was preserved.

| Metric | Baseline | This PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Draft shards | 49 | 1 |
| TP0 draft-load median | 2.34s | **0.99s** |
| TP0 draft-load range | 2.32–2.38s | 0.95–1.03s |
| Slowest-rank draft-load median | 2.68s | **1.34s** |
| Slowest-rank draft-load range | 2.64–2.73s | 1.30–1.37s |

All ten launches passed health checks and completed two fixed generation requests each. The draft-stage reduction was repeatable; main loading still selected all 49 shards.

Median engine-start-to-HTTP-health time was **265.06s → 268.07s**, so these runs do not establish an overall startup improvement. This interval includes initialization, compilation, and warmup, but excludes checkpoint preparation.

### Regression coverage

Regression coverage includes real safetensors files, selection before iterator/prefetch construction, mixed shards, shared weights, pipeline-parallel embeddings, layer-selection rules, and fallback for incompatible name transformations. Generation requests are serving-function checks, not model-accuracy evaluations.

## Scope and downstream reuse

This PR provides the model-selection interface and Default Loader integration. A companion PR applies the same interface to the separate RunAI ModelStreamer path. The reference vLLM #60152 does not cover RunAI; the corresponding vLLM RunAI integration is [#60759](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60759).

This PR does not change model execution, scheduling, RunAI internals, or MX P2P. It also does not change Hugging Face downloads that happen before local file resolution. MX can reuse this optimization through a framework loader entry point that passes the actual model and its selection rule, without maintaining separate checkpoint-naming rules.

## Accuracy Tests

The generation-request checks described above verify serving behavior, not a full model-quality evaluation. This change does not modify model forward computation.

## Local validation

- Pre-commit on the changed files: passed.
- Documentation build validation and broken-link checks: passed.
- Added registered SGLang tests for model-owned selection, loader integration, and compatibility fallback.
## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

@hzh0425 Thanks for your patience.

To clarify the feature scope: this PR extracts the existing main/MTP weight-selection rules from the models’ `load_weights` methods into reusable functions. Default Loader then uses these rules to skip wholly unused safetensors shards before reading weight data or starting prefetch, avoiding unnecessary reads of weights that would otherwise be discarded. This feature does not change model computation, parameter mapping, quantization, or parallel sharding.

I reviewed the failed jobs against their actual CI checkouts and compared them with runs on main and other PRs. Several failures have causes outside the MTP filtering change:

- The Flux image-comparison failure also occurs in merged #47488. Upstream #46947 identified ROCm VAE convolution nondeterminism, and its [patched CI run passed the same exact comparison](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40814705814/job/123253072366).
- The H20 health-check failed with a GitHub API 502. The MUSA checkout/source-clone failures were GitHub connection/TLS errors. These failures all occurred before model tests.
- The PP auxiliary-data transfer timeout also [occurred on main](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39996824937/job/120562479214) before this branch’s Mooncake registration fix. The failing PP/NPU models do not implement the new MTP selection hook; local differential tests confirmed unchanged checkpoint selection and loader dispatch for those paths.

To address these CI issues, I consolidated the latest verified fixes into one additional commit, [2c2144f](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/2c2144f0e676b642b8ef68900a1b5ea5018698b3):

- Added the missing MUSA `ml-dtypes` runtime dependency.
- Backported the ROCm VAE determinism fix from #46947.
- Backported the paired test-runner API changes from merged #47592, fixing the `fork_worker_preload` mismatch between merge-checkout tests and the PR-installed package.

Focused local regression tests pass, and the original accuracy assertions are preserved. PP/NPU still need hardware validation: an interaction between the PP registration change and transport behavior has not been ruled out, and the NPU pinned-memory allocation failure is not yet fully explained.

Could you please help rerun the relevant CI and investigate the remaining PP/NPU issues? Thank you!

@hzh0425 Thanks for your patience.

I’ve rebased this PR onto `main` and pushed the updated version, `66ab174`. The diff now contains only the MTP checkpoint-selection changes and their supporting tests and documentation: extracting the existing weight-selection rules into reusable helpers and applying them before Default Loader reads unused shards.

Several issues behind the earlier CI failures have now been addressed upstream, including:

- ROCm VAE convolution determinism for the Flux exact-image comparison ([#46947](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46947)).
- The test-runner `fork_worker_preload` API mismatch ([#47592](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/47592)).
- NIXL storage-test interference from background eviction ([#47197](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/47197)).

These upstream changes are included through the rebase. I’ve removed the separate CI repair patches from this branch; CI workflows, dependencies, and non-MTP runtime code now match `main`.

I’ve posted `/rerun-failed-ci`, but the workflows still require maintainer approval. Could you please approve the CI workflows for `66ab174` so we can validate the updated version? Thank you!

+"""Model-owned MTP checkpoint selection, without allocating model weights."""
+
+import unittest
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=10, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+def _without_weights(model_class, **config):
+    model = model_class.__new__(model_class)
+    torch.nn.Module.__init__(model)
+    model.config = SimpleNamespace(**config)
+    return model
+
+
+class TestQwenCheckpointSelection(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_qwen3_moe_main_and_draft_filter_their_own_weights(self):
+        from sglang.srt.models.qwen3_moe import Qwen3MoeForCausalLM
+        from sglang.srt.models.qwen3_moe_mtp import Qwen3MoeForCausalLMMTP
+
+        main = _without_weights(Qwen3MoeForCausalLM)
+        draft = _without_weights(Qwen3MoeForCausalLMMTP)
+        for name, main_unused, draft_unused in (
+            ("model.layers.0.mlp.gate_proj.weight", False, True),
+            ("mtp.layers.0.mlp.gate_proj.weight", True, False),
+            ("mtp.fc.weight", True, False),
+            ("mtp.layers.0.rotary_emb.inv_freq", True, True),
+        ):
+            with self.subTest(name=name):
+                self.assertEqual(main.is_unused_checkpoint_weight(name), main_unused)
+                self.assertEqual(draft.is_unused_checkpoint_weight(name), draft_unused)
+
+    def test_qwen4_main_skips_draft_weights_without_skipping_vision_shards(self):
+        from sglang.srt.models.qwen4_exp import Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration
+        from sglang.srt.models.qwen4_exp_mtp import Qwen4ExpForCausalLMMTP
+
+        main = _without_weights(Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration)
+        main.language_model_only = True
+        draft = _without_weights(Qwen4ExpForCausalLMMTP)
+        for name, main_unused, draft_unused in (
+            ("model.language_model.layers.0.self_attn.q_proj.weight", False, True),
+            ("mtp.layers.0.self_attn.q_proj.weight", True, False),
+            ("model.language_model.embed_tokens.weight", False, False),
+            ("model.visual.blocks.0.attn.qkv.weight", False, True),
+            ("mtp.layers.0.rotary_emb.inv_freq", True, True),
+        ):
+            with self.subTest(name=name):
+                self.assertEqual(main.is_unused_checkpoint_weight(name), main_unused)
+                self.assertEqual(draft.is_unused_checkpoint_weight(name), draft_unused)
+
+    def test_qwen35_main_and_draft_use_distinct_rules(self):
+        from sglang.srt.models.qwen3_5 import (
+            Qwen3_5ForCausalLM,
+            Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration,
+            Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM,
+            Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration,
+        )
+        from sglang.srt.models.qwen3_5_mtp import Qwen3_5ForCausalLMMTP
+        from sglang.srt.models.qwen3_5_text import (
+            Qwen3_5ForCausalLM as Qwen3_5TextForCausalLM,
+        )
+
+        cases = [
+            ("model.layers.0.self_attn.q_proj.weight", False, True),
+            ("mtp.layers.0.self_attn.q_proj.weight", True, False),
+            ("mtp.layers.0.mlp.experts.0.up_proj.weight_scale", True, False),
+            ("mtp.fc.weight", True, False),
+            ("model.embed_tokens.weight", False, False),
+            ("model.language_model.embed_tokens.weight", False, False),
+            ("lm_head.weight", False, True),
+            ("mtp.layers.0.rotary_emb.inv_freq", True, True),
+        ]
+        for cls in (
+            Qwen3_5ForCausalLM,
+            Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration,
+            Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM,
+            Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration,

+                    )
+                    self.assertEqual(
+                        draft.is_unused_checkpoint_weight(name), draft_unused
+                    )
+
+    def test_qwen_next_does_not_inherit_qwen35_embedding_exception(self):

@hzh0425 Thanks for your patience.

To clarify the feature scope: this PR extracts the existing main/MTP weight-selection rules from the models’ `load_weights` methods into reusable functions. Default Loader then uses these rules to skip wholly unused safetensors shards before reading weight data or starting prefetch, avoiding unnecessary reads of weights that would otherwise be discarded. This feature does not change model computation, parameter mapping, quantization, or parallel sharding.

I reviewed the failed jobs against their actual CI checkouts and compared them with runs on main and other PRs. Several failures have causes outside the MTP filtering change:
